content: 1. At the time of passing the bills, the title was updated to The Repealing and Amending (Third) Bill (2015). 2. The Global Leprosy Strategy 2016–2020 outlines specific targets and indicators, referred to as core programmatic indicators, which all leprosy programs worldwide are required to collect routinely, regardless of the disease burden or local context. 3. Visible deformities in the eyes, hands, and feet are recorded in patient records available at various administrative levels, including national, state, province, district, village, urban areas, and health centers. Pediatric cases with Grade 2 Disability (G2D) are enumerated at the end of the reporting year and reported as absolute numbers annually. This data reflects the quality of leprosy detection and community awareness of early symptoms and signs. 4. Target 2 aims to reduce new leprosy cases with G2D to less than one case per million population. This is calculated by dividing the number of newly diagnosed G2D cases by the mid-year population and multiplying by 1,000,000. This target applies globally and nationally to countries with populations exceeding one million. 5. Target 3 seeks to eliminate countries with legislation that allows discrimination based on leprosy. This involves identifying and reporting the number of legal provisions, laws, or practices that permit discrimination against individuals affected by leprosy and their families. The data is sourced from national publications, gazettes, and legal documents. 6. The annual new case detection rate (NCDR) measures the number of new leprosy cases per 100,000 population. This is calculated by dividing the number of new cases by the mid-year population and multiplying by 100,000. It serves as a proxy for leprosy incidence in a given area. 7. Prevalence refers to the number of leprosy cases under treatment at a specific point in time during the year. This data is used to calculate multidrug therapy (MDT) requirements and reflects the magnitude of the leprosy burden in a given area. 8. The point prevalence rate (PR) measures the number of registered leprosy cases on MDT per 10,000 population. It is calculated by dividing the number of cases by the mid-year population and multiplying by 10,000. This indicator helps assess the leprosy burden and MDT needs in areas with populations of at least 10,000. 9. The proportion of Grade 2 Disability (G2D) cases among new cases indicates the percentage of new leprosy cases detected with G2D at registration for MDT. This reflects the capacity to detect leprosy early, as a high percentage is associated with delayed diagnosis. 10. The proportion of pediatric cases among new cases measures the percentage of new leprosy cases detected in children under 15 years of age. This indicator is sensitive to transmission trends and reflects the level of leprosy transmission in a given area. 11. The proportion of multibacillary (MB) cases among new cases measures the percentage of leprosy cases classified as MB at registration for MDT. This reflects the magnitude of the leprosy problem and the capacity for early detection, as effective health services should detect cases when they are predominantly paucibacillary (PB). 12. The proportion of female cases among new cases measures the percentage of females diagnosed with leprosy and registered for MDT. This reflects the accessibility of leprosy services for women and indirectly informs the quality of services provided. 13. The proportion of foreign-born cases among new cases measures the percentage of foreign-born individuals diagnosed with leprosy and registered for MDT. This reflects local transmission and the accessibility of leprosy services for foreign-born individuals. 14. The number of relapses in a year measures the total number of leprosy cases diagnosed as relapses during the reporting year. This reflects the quality of treatment services and may indicate the circulation of drug-resistant strains if the number increases. 15. The treatment completion/cure rate of MB cases measures the proportion of MB cases completing MDT within 18 months of starting treatment. This is calculated through cohort analysis and reflects the quality of services provided and the accessibility of leprosy services. 16. The treatment completion/cure rate of PB cases measures the proportion of PB cases completing MDT within 9 months of starting treatment. This is also calculated through cohort analysis and reflects the quality and accessibility of leprosy services. 17. The percentage of household contacts screened among registered household contacts measures the proportion of household contacts of registered patients screened for leprosy during the year. This data is sourced from patient records and reflects the effectiveness of contact screening programs.
